subject: Hosted vs Reserved capacity — latency & volume signal request (FastLedger)
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Amira Hassan <amira@fastledger.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-09T15:02:00Z
Subject: Hosted vs Reserved capacity — quick follow-up and signal ask

Hi Amira,

Thanks again for the call earlier — really helpful to hear how FastLedger's transaction enrichment flows operate. To make a crisp recommendation between Redwood Hosted API and Reserved (Dedicated) capacity, we need a few concrete workload signals from your side. Would you be able to confirm the items below? If you prefer, you can drop the numbers in the attached RFI spreadsheet.

Key signals we need:
- Typical sustained QPS (requests/sec) and expected peak QPS (1–5 minute windows)
- 95th and 99th token-generation latency targets (ms) for inference (user-facing SLO)
- Average input + context token count and max context length you expect to pass
- Typical payload size (kb) and whether you use streaming responses
- Burst concurrency profile (how often do you hit peak bursts per day/week)
- Any strict network requirements: private VPC, on-prem, or SOC2/PCI constraints

Quick take from our end based on today: if your 95th latency SLO is <=150ms at sustained hundreds of qps, Dedicated reserved capacity is usually the fastest/most predictable route; if your peaks are short and you value self-serve, Hosted with autoscale and caching will often be cheaper.

Next steps: if you send the signals above I’ll loop in pricing and infra owners and propose a short pilot plan (benchmarks + canary rollout). I attached a short RFI and the call recording for reference.

Cheers,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Amira Hassan <amira@fastledger.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-09T19:14:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Reserved capacity — quick follow-up and signal ask

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and for the call. Below are the signals you requested; I populated the RFI and attached it as well. High level: latency is a hard constraint for us for customer-facing enrichment. Security is important but not an immediate blocker for pilot.

Signals (from our production expectations):
- Sustained QPS: 180 req/sec (baseline). Peak QPS: 1,000 req/sec for 3–5 minute bursts during batch releases (approx 2–3x weekly).
- 95th latency SLO: 120ms for the inference step (end-to-end enrichment budget is 200ms). 99th we aim for <300ms.
- Avg tokens per request: ~350 tokens total (input + context). Max context anticipated: 2,048 tokens.
- Typical payload: ~28KB JSON. We do use streaming for long responses in a subset of flows.
- Burst pattern: predictable spikes during deploys and morning syncs; short-lived but frequent.
- Compliance: SOC 2 required, PCI-scoped PII redaction planned; long term we may require VPC peering but for the pilot we can use hosted with contract-level controls.

I've attached FastLedger_RFI_filled.xlsx. Let me know if anything else helps. We’re interested in a recommendation that balances predictability for latency with cost.

Best,
Amira Hassan
Head of Platform Engineering | FastLedger
amira@fastledger.com

Attachments: FastLedger_RFI_filled.xlsx (spreadsheet, 38KB)

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-06-10T01:06:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Hosted vs Reserved capacity — signals from FastLedger (recommendation + asks)

Looping you both in — Amira sent final signals (attached). Quick internal read:

- Workload: baseline ~180 QPS, predictable peaks ~1,000 QPS for 3–5 minutes several times per week.
- Latency SLO: 95th = 120ms (tight), 99th <300ms. Avg tokens ~350; max 2k context.
- Security: SOC 2 required; VPC likely later but pilot can run on Hosted with contractual protections.

Tentative recommendation: run a short Dedicated reserved pilot sized to cover sustained baseline with headroom for short burst capacity plus configured hosted fallback for excess burst (to avoid dropped requests). This gives predictable 95th latency and control over model colocations (KV cache, batch sizing).

Proposed next steps:
1) Rishi — can you draft two pricing options: a 3-month pilot reserved capacity plan sized for 200 sustained QPS + burst buffer vs a hybrid (smaller reserved + hosted burst) with estimated token-cost delta? Please include estimated lead time for capacity reservations.
2) Marissa — can your infra team run a 2-hour benchmark matrix (200, 500, 1k QPS) on our standard Llama-derived model variant with 350-token average payload? We need measured 95th latency and cost-per-token for each point. Can we schedule that this week or next?
3) Alex — I’ll coordinate ask items and propose a pilot timeline to FastLedger (benchmarks, canary routing, rollback plan).

Amira — cc'd here so you're aware of the proposed path. If you'd prefer we can scope a pure Hosted pilot first, but given the 120ms SLO I suspect Dedicated will be the safer baseline.

Thanks,
Alex

Attachments referenced: FastLedger_RFI_filled.xlsx (from customer), session-recording-20270609.mp3 (call)
